title: NEMAR recipe progress file, nemar.recipe-progress.v1
description: The file a job writes at $NEMAR_OUT/.nemar-progress/progress.json while it runs, which the launcher reads from outside the container to report live progress and, in standalone mode, to build the results report (ADR 0134 decisions 3 and 8). Copied byte for byte from nemarOrg/nemar-cli (shared/contract/compute-recipe-progress.schema.json) by nemarOrg/nemar-process (launcher/schema/compute-recipe-progress.v1.json). It holds the recipe and its checkpoint map, the recordings table relative to NEMAR_OUT, how many recordings the run discovered, and the running recording with its step; no samples and no host path. The file is at most 65536 bytes. Together with these encoding rules, which no schema can state, the schema describes exactly what the launcher's reader accepts: the text is UTF-8 JSON with no duplicate key, no NaN, Infinity or -Infinity, and every integer written without a fraction (1, never 1.0). The root has no constraint; each shape is a member of $defs. Rules a schema cannot state, the reader's: a checkpoint is named once, and a step is in one checkpoint only. CheckpointName, StepId and Count are compute-progress-v1.json's own.

CheckpointName.description: A checkpoint a recipe declares (neuroschema processingTypes checkpointName).

CheckpointMap.description: A recipe's checkpoint map: 1 to 8 checkpoints in the order the recipe declares them, each with 1 to 64 steps in order. stored is never declared (the backend sets it). Rules a schema cannot state, the reader's: a checkpoint is named once, and a step is in one checkpoint only.

table.description: The recordings table, relative to NEMAR_OUT: 1 to 8 /-separated parts, each a letter or digit then up to 127 letters, digits, ., _ or -, the last ending in _recordings.tsv.

discovered.description: How many recordings the run discovered; every one gets exactly one row in the recordings table.

running.description: The recording that is running, if any, and the step it is in (null until its first step starts).
